[=Value Model=]

[.txt|mVM_Data.tData.] is the only runtime representation.

The data kinds currently used are:

- [.txt|Empty.]
- [.txt|Bool.]
- [.txt|Int.]
- [.txt|Pair.]
- [.txt|Prefix.]
- [.txt|Record.]
- [.txt|Proc.]
- [.txt|ExternProc.]
- [.txt|Def.]
- [.txt|ExternDef.]
- [.txt|Var.]
- [.txt|Type.]

[.mermaid
|flowchart TD
|	DATA["mVM_Data.tData"] --> PRIM["Empty / Bool / Int"]
|	DATA --> STRUCT["Pair / Prefix / Record"]
|	DATA --> CODE["Def / Proc / ExternDef / ExternProc"]
|	DATA --> MUT["Var"]
|	DATA --> TYPE["Type"]
.]

Important architectural decision:

- complex values are modeled mostly through [.txt|Pair.], [.txt|Prefix.], and [.txt|Record.]
- tuples are only sugar over pairs
- text values are runtime-level recursive char lists

[=Register Contract=]

Every call stack starts with a fixed register layout.

[| [*Index*] | [*Meaning*] | [*Source*] |]
[| [.txt|0.] | [.txt|EMPTY.] | fixed runtime value |]
[| [.txt|1.] | [.txt|ONE.] | helper value for integer arithmetic |]
[| [.txt|2.] | [.txt|FALSE.] | boolean constant |]
[| [.txt|3.] | [.txt|TRUE.] | boolean constant |]
[| [.txt|4.] | [.txt|EMPTY_TYPE.] | type value |]
[| [.txt|5.] | [.txt|BOOL_TYPE.] | type value |]
[| [.txt|6.] | [.txt|INT_TYPE.] | type value |]
[| [.txt|7.] | [.txt|TYPE_TYPE.] | type value |]
[| [.txt|8.] | [.txt|ENV.] | proc environment |]
[| [.txt|9.] | [.txt|OBJ.] | object for method calls |]
[| [.txt|10.] | [.txt|ARG.] | argument |]
[| [.txt|11.] | [.txt|RES.] | result slot |]

This layout is created in [.txt|mVM.NewCallStack(...).] and assumed by [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.].

[=Module Startup in the VM=]

[.txt|mVM.Run(mIL_AST.tModule, ...).] starts a module using a fixed contract:

- [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.GenerateOpcodes(...).] produces an ordered list of [.txt|tProcDef.]
- the last def is the module initializer
- all earlier defs are packed into [.txt|ENV.] as a [.txt|Def.] tuple
- the resolved import record is placed into [.txt|ARG.]
- [.txt|OBJ.] is always [.txt|().] when a module starts

[=Proc, Def, and Call Model=]

[.mermaid
|sequenceDiagram
|	participant Caller
|	participant VM
|	participant Proc as tProcDef
|
|	Caller->>VM: Proc + ENV + OBJ + ARG + RES
|	VM->>Proc: start at command 0
|	loop until return or match failure
|		Proc->>VM: execute opcode
|	end
|	VM-->>Caller: RES filled or case discarded
.]

Important differences:

- [.txt|Def.] is an unbound definition
- [.txt|Proc.] is a definition plus environment
- [.txt|ExternDef.] and [.txt|ExternProc.] allow host functions without IL
- [.txt|CallFunc.] invokes functions without an object; when given a [.txt|Def.], it first materializes a [.txt|Proc.] by binding the passed argument as new environment
- [.txt|CallProc.] invokes methods with [.txt|(Obj, Proc).] pairs and stores the object in register [.txt|OBJ.]

[.txt|ReturnIf.] writes into [.txt|RES.] and ends the current stack frame.

[=Pattern Matching in the Runtime=]

Match semantics are prepared during lowering, but not every exposed opcode is executable yet.

- opcodes defined in IL / opcode generation:
  [.txt|TryAsEmpty.], [.txt|TryAsBool.], [.txt|TryAsInt.], [.txt|TryAsType.], [.txt|TryAsPair.], [.txt|TryAsRecord.], [.txt|TryAsVar.], [.txt|TryAsRef.], [.txt|TryRemovePrefixFrom.]
- opcodes actually executed in [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] today:
  [.txt|TryAsEmpty.], [.txt|TryAsBool.], [.txt|TryAsInt.], [.txt|TryAsPair.], [.txt|TryAsRecord.], [.txt|TryAsVar.], [.txt|TryRemovePrefixFrom.]

Current gap:

- [.txt|TryAsType.] is parsed, represented, and emitted, but not executed by the VM
- [.txt|TryAsRef.] has the same problem, and [.txt|mVM_Data.tDataType.] currently has no [.txt|Ref.] runtime value kind

[=Type Values at Runtime=]

The VM can move [.txt|Type.] data around, but this area still has a real three-layer gap:

- [.txt|mVM_Data.tOpCode.] defines a wider family of runtime type constructors
- [.txt|mIL_GenerateOpcodes.] can already emit more runtime type-building commands than the VM executes
- [.txt|mVM.Step(...).] currently executes only a subset of those [.txt|Type*.] opcodes

That means compile-time type work is more mature than runtime type evaluation.

[=Modules Registered in Code=]

[.txt|mModule.cs.] currently exposes:

- [.txt|Module_Std.] from [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/Std.ILT.]
- [.txt|Module_Char.] from [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/Char.SPO.], depending on [.txt|Std.]
- [.txt|Module_Text.] from [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/Text.SPO.], depending on [.txt|Std.] and [.txt|Char.]
- [.txt|Module_Maybe.] from [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/Maybe.SPO.]

The [.txt|Modules/.] folder contains more artifacts than the registry exposes:

- [.txt|Std.ILT.]
- [.txt|Char.SPO.] and [.txt|Char.ILT.]
- [.txt|Text.SPO.] and [.txt|Text.ILT.]
- [.txt|Maybe.SPO.] and [.txt|Maybe.ILT.]
- [.txt|Result.SPO.]

Only the four [.txt|Module_*.] values above are addressable through [.txt|mModule.] today.

Use [<../40_verification/41_tests_and_artifacts.wiki|41_tests_and_artifacts.wiki>] for the current green/red state of those modules.

[=Observable Module Semantics=]

The registered modules are layered this way:

- [.txt|Std.] provides arithmetic and boolean core operations
- [.txt|Char.] builds character comparison and character functions on top of that
- [.txt|Text.] builds recursive text functions on top of [.txt|Char.]
- [.txt|Maybe.] is part of the registered module path and therefore part of module-boundary verification

[=Host Embedding Example=]

Outside [.txt|SPO_CS/.], [.txt|SPO/src/Program.cs.] shows how the runtime is embedded by a host application:

- it initializes [.txt|Module_Std.]
- it exposes [.txt|_StdLib.] as imported runtime data
- it exposes [.txt|_LoadModule....] as an [.txt|ExternProc.]
- it expects the loaded SPO program to produce a callable value that is then executed with object [.txt|#IO ().]
